cover.headline: Bajaj's favourite supplier at a fair price: the growth is real, the margins are the catch
cover.lead: Endurance makes aluminium castings, suspension, brakes and transmission parts for Indian two-wheelers (Bajaj Auto alone is 35% of income) and machined castings for European carmakers (27%). Revenue grew 17% a year over FY21-26 and 30% in Q1FY27, but net profit only 8% as metal costs ran ahead of price resets and Europe wrote off old engine-programme assets. We forecast EPS of ₹75.3 / ₹90.0 / ₹101.0 for FY27-29E, below the street. The street values Endurance on **P/E on one-year-forward EPS** (MOSL 32x and Choice 30x FY28E). The house rule (its own forward P/E median since 2021, 31.3x, cut by the 7.8% auto-component de-rating) gives **29x Sep-28E EPS of ₹95.5 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with HOLD.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹2,842, DCF ₹1,930. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: India standalone income rose 20% in FY26 and 36% in Q1FY27 (~24% without metal pass-through) against 2W sales growth of 13% and 24%. Sales to Bajaj grew 16% in FY26 vs Bajaj's own 12%; to Honda 17% vs 8%. The drivers are content: brakes (+30% a year for four years; ABS capacity doubling), inverted front forks, alloy wheels (Bidkin plant), and new lines (battery packs from Jun-2026, 4W castings for a US EV maker and JLR). Orders won since FY23: ₹5,270 cr a year at peak, excluding Bajaj. We model India +{{as.segments.0.growth.0|pct0}} / +{{as.segments.0.growth.1|pct0}} / +{{as.segments.0.growth.2|pct0}}.

arguments.h: But India's margin is hostage to metal prices and to Bajaj
arguments.p: Aluminium is ~60% of purchases and is passed on a quarter late, at cost: in Q1FY27 raw materials rose to 68.4% of standalone income and the India EBITDA margin fell to 11.2% (12.6% in FY26, 13.7% in FY25). Management says Q2 and Q3 will be "better than Q1", without a number. Bajaj Auto takes 35% of group income (38% in FY25): the relationship is deep, but the customer sets the price. We assume {{as.segments.0.marginPct.0|pct}} / {{as.segments.0.marginPct.1|pct}} / {{as.segments.0.marginPct.2|pct}}.

arguments.h: Europe: high margins, little organic growth
arguments.p: Endurance Overseas (Italy, Germany) earns an ~18% EBITDA margin, but its euro revenue grew 2% in FY26 without the Stöferle purchase and 1% in Q1FY27, while European car production fell 5% and Chinese brands took the growth. A Mercedes hybrid part (100% share from Jan-2027) helps; combustion-engine programmes (~30% of sales) run off. We assume euro revenue +2% / +5% / +4% and an 18.0-18.3% margin; management talks openly about more European acquisitions.

arguments.h: Valuation: fair; the gap to the street is earnings
arguments.p: At ₹2,657 the stock trades at 29.5x our FY28E and 27.8x Sep-28E EPS, just below its own 31.3x forward median since 2021; auto-component stocks sat 7.8% below their five-year medians on 30-Sep-2026. The street's 30-32x is similar to ours; its targets (₹3,350-3,380) are higher because its FY28E EPS (₹108.8 median) is 21% above ours: it assumes margins recover to ~14% and European depreciation normalises fast. We would rather see the margin first.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): whether India margins recover as Q1-average metal rates and gas, fuel and wage claims are settled with customers, as management promised.
ABS: the government's final rule on ABS for smaller motorcycles (draft Jun-2025); new ABS/CBS capacity starting Sep/Oct-2026; dual-channel ABS for Bajaj (Q2FY27) and a second programme (Q3FY27).
Ramp-ups: Shendra 4W machined castings (SOP Sep-2026; ₹513 cr a year at peak by early FY29), Bidkin alloy wheels at full capacity by Q4FY27, battery-pack line full by Oct-2026, Chennai brakes plant.
Europe: the Mercedes hybrid programme from Jan-2027; a casting-capacity deal for Stöferle by Jan-2027; any acquisition ("more clarity in the next investor call").
Festive-season two-wheeler volumes (Oct-Dec 2026) against a GST-boosted base, and Bajaj Auto's market share.

sections.title: Two businesses under one roof: Indian two-wheeler parts (72%) and European car castings (27%)

blocks.p: Endurance Technologies is an Aurangabad-born (now Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar) tier-1 supplier controlled by the Jain family (75%) and run by Managing Director Anurang Jain. It has 34 plants. **In India** (the listed company, "standalone") it makes aluminium die-castings and alloy wheels, suspension (front forks, shock absorbers), braking systems (disc brakes, ABS, 3W and 4W brakes), transmission parts (clutches, driveshafts) and, since Jun-2026, electric-scooter battery packs; ~70% of India income comes from motorcycles. It holds 44% of India's two-wheeler front-fork market, 37% of shock absorbers, 34.5% of brake assemblies and 42% of brake discs (FY26). **Maxwell** (100%) designs battery-management electronics. **In Europe** Endurance Overseas (Italy, and Germany through Stöferle, 68% owned after Q1FY27) makes machined aluminium castings, mostly for VW group, Mercedes and Stellantis, plus 2W brakes and clutches. By vehicle, FY26 income was 52.1% motorcycles, 29% four-wheelers (mostly Europe), 8.6% scooters and 8% three-wheelers; by product, 46.6% die-casting, 24.7% suspension, 11.5% brakes and 7.2% alloy wheels.

sections.title: Forty years from two casting machines: licences first, then acquisitions in Italy and Germany

blocks.p: Endurance began in 1985 with two aluminium die-casting machines in Aurangabad and grew by adding products the same customer bought: suspension, transmission and brakes, each started with a European technology partner (Paioli, Adler, Grimeca, later KTM for premium forks). From 2006 it bought small European casting and brake makers, which became Endurance Overseas, and in April 2025 its largest deal: 60% of Germany's Stöferle for EUR37.7 mn, with the rest bought 8% a year to 2030 at a price linked to Stöferle's EBITDA. The group listed in October 2016. The share count has not changed since FY17, so EPS growth equals profit growth.

sections.title: India: record two-wheeler sales (+23.6% in Q1FY27). Europe: registrations up, production down

blocks.p: India sold 26.89 mn two-wheelers in FY26 (+12.9%: motorcycles +10.5%, scooters +18.6%), 1.3 mn three-wheelers (+23.7%) and 6.72 mn four-wheelers (+10%). The September 2025 GST cut on small two-wheelers lifted the second half, and Q1FY27 was a record: 7.18 mn two-wheelers (+23.6%; scooters +32.7%), three-wheelers +40%, four-wheelers +22.7%. From Q3FY27 the comparison base includes the GST boost. In Europe, new-car registrations rose 3.3% in FY26 and 7.4% in Q1FY27, but only ~3% excluding Chinese brands, and production fell 5%; battery-electric cars were 21.9% of registrations and hybrids of all kinds ~46%.

bullets: **India: the tailwind reaches it, and it adds content on top.** Sales to each big customer grew 5-9 points faster than that customer's volumes in FY26.
**But part of Q1's growth was metal.** Of the 35.9% standalone growth, ~12.9 points was higher raw-material cost passed through at no margin.

**Europe: no tailwind.** Organic growth is near zero; Stöferle made FY26 look strong. The order book is being rebuilt around hybrids and EVs (86% of orders won in five years), but the run-off of combustion-engine work comes first.

sections.title: India: two-wheeler content keeps growing; the margin depends on how fast metal costs are passed on

blocks.p: India (the listed company's standalone accounts) earned ₹10,696 cr of total income in FY26 (+20%) at a 12.6% EBITDA margin (13.7% in FY25). Q1FY27 income was ₹3,194 cr (+35.9%), but raw materials rose to 68.4% of income (64.8% a year earlier) and the margin fell to 11.2%. Management's explanation: Q1 was billed on Q4FY26 metal prices while it paid Q1 prices (>₹300 cr up front); excluding the non-value-add metal increase, the margin would have been 13.33%. From Q2 customers pay Q1-average rates, aluminium alloy has softened by ₹12-17/kg, and gas, fuel and wage increases are being negotiated. The standalone business still had ₹416 cr of net cash at Jun-2026.

sections.title: Europe: an 18% margin business with no organic growth; Stöferle bought the growth

blocks.p: Endurance Overseas made EUR391.7 mn of total income in FY26 (+28.9%) and EUR72.4 mn of EBITDA (18.5%). Without Stöferle, income grew 2% (parts only: +6.4%). Stöferle, bought on 2-Apr-2025, contributed EUR82.1 mn of income, EUR17.9 mn of EBITDA and EUR8 mn of profit, a little better than planned, plus ~EUR20 mn of cash. In Q1FY27 income was EUR104.3 mn (+1.1%) and EBITDA EUR18.9 mn (18.2%), but profit fell to EUR4.4 mn from EUR6.4 mn because Endurance is writing off, over ~18 months, the remaining value of machines tied to combustion-engine programmes that are ending (depreciation EUR11.6 mn vs EUR8.5 mn). Orders won: EUR15.8 mn in FY26 and EUR13.9 mn in Q1FY27, including a Mercedes hybrid-transmission part where Endurance takes 100% of the volume from Jan-2027 after a rival went bankrupt (~EUR40 mn a year, MOSL).

bullets: **Why the margin is high:** machined castings for premium German brands (VW-Audi-Porsche 7.8% of group income, Mercedes 7.4%), indexed metal prices (quarterly, on the previous quarter's average) and support from customers when energy costs spiked.

**Why growth is low:** European car production fell 5% in Q1FY27; Chinese brands import their powertrains; combustion-engine work (~30% of Europe sales) runs down to ~25% by FY28; Stöferle buys its castings from outside and its full integration benefit starts only from Sep-2027.

**What could change it:** acquisitions ("good companies available at good prices", MD) and work moved from bankrupt suppliers. The put/call price for the rest of Stöferle rises with its EBITDA above EUR17 mn (4.5x the excess), so the better Stöferle does, the more the remaining 32% costs.

sections.title: Electronics and battery packs: small today, the main source of new content

blocks.p: Maxwell (BMS, motor controllers, telematics, DC-DC converters) had ₹161 cr of income in FY26 (₹70 cr in FY25) and turned its first profit in Q1FY27 (₹1 cr; income ₹57 cr, +85%). It supplied ~1 lakh BMS units in the quarter to scooter, 3W, tractor and construction-equipment makers; cumulative orders are ₹238 cr a year at peak (Q2FY28) with ₹300 cr+ of quotes outstanding. The bigger change is in the standalone business: a battery-pack plant near Pune started supplying Hero MotoCorp in June 2026, using Maxwell's BMS and Endurance's castings, with a 4W battery pack to follow in Q4FY27. Management will not yet give a battery-pack margin; it is "a very high-value business" where the target is the company's average margin.

sections.title: Bajaj Auto: 35% of income, falling slowly as other customers and Europe grow

blocks.p: Bajaj Auto bought 35% of the group's FY26 income (38% in FY25, 39.4% in FY24). If, as we assume, nearly all of it is billed from India, Bajaj is roughly half of standalone income (~₹5,150 cr of ₹10,696 cr; the company does not disclose the standalone share). The relationship goes back to the company's start, and Endurance gains share inside Bajaj (FY26: sales to Bajaj +16% vs Bajaj volumes +12%), including EV programmes, ABS and alloy wheels. The order statistics Endurance publishes exclude Bajaj, so they understate total new business. The risk is the mirror image: Bajaj sets prices, delays metal pass-through by a quarter, and any loss of Bajaj's market share (motorcycles are ~70% of India income, against a market moving to scooters) flows straight to Endurance.

blocks.title: Moat scorecard
blocks.source: GAM research compilation (annual report, presentations and calls to Aug-2026; broker notes)

blocks.callout: **Verdict: a narrow moat.** Endurance has real advantages in Indian two-wheeler suspension and brakes: the largest share, 15-25 years of programmes with each customer, in-house testing and now ABS electronics. Switching a supplier of safety parts is slow, which shows up in steady share gains. But it has no pricing power (metal is passed through at cost, late), depends on one customer for a third of income, and its European castings business competes on cost and capacity in a shrinking market.

sections.title: Revenue nearly three times in a decade; margins slipped from 16% to 13% as metal costs and Europe diluted them

blocks.p: Endurance's revenue was ₹4,917 cr in FY15 and ₹14,596 cr in FY26: 10% a year over eleven years, 17% a year since the Covid year FY21. Two things drove it: Indian two-wheeler content (suspension, brakes, ABS, alloy wheels on more and bigger bikes) and Europe, where the Stöferle purchase in April 2025 alone added ~₹840 cr in FY26 (EUR82 mn). Margins went the other way: EBITDA was 15-16% of revenue in FY19-21 and 12-14% since FY22, because aluminium prices rose (metal cost passed through at cost inflates revenue but not profit) and European energy prices tripled from 2021 levels. EPS went from ₹35 (FY19, the pre-Covid high) to ₹68 (FY26), 10% a year; from FY21, 13% a year.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** Endurance is a steady grower with good, not great, returns. ROE fell from 20-23% before Covid to 11-16% since FY22: margins dropped, the balance sheet carries ~₹1,900 cr of cash and investments, and Europe earns high EBITDA margins but needs heavy depreciation. The earnings line that matters most is India's margin, which swings with how fast aluminium and steel costs are passed on to Bajaj Auto and other two-wheeler makers.

**Orders:** India ₹391.6 cr in Q1 (excl. Bajaj; ₹336 cr from Honda, incl. a ₹220 cr higher-margin suspension facelift); ₹10.5 cr more from the US EV maker (now ₹223 cr a year); RFQs ₹4,526 cr.

The bear case assumes metal and energy stay high and customers pay late.

sections.title: Self-funded growth: ₹4,724 cr of capex and ₹520 cr of acquisitions in six years, still net cash

blocks.p: Over FY21-26 Endurance generated ₹6,665 cr of operating cash, spent ₹4,724 cr on capex, ₹520 cr on acquisitions (Maxwell, Frenotecnica and New Fren, Stöferle) and paid ₹531 cr of dividends (payout 16-21%). It stayed net cash throughout: ₹579 cr at Mar-2026 (cash and investments ₹1,906 cr less borrowings ₹1,327 cr), plus a ₹246 cr deferred liability for the rest of Stöferle. India capex is guided at ~₹800 cr in FY27, the same as FY26, spread across brakes, ABS, alloy wheels, castings and battery packs; Europe spent EUR45 mn in FY26. Returns: ROCE 17-18% on Screener's basis in FY24-26, below the 21-25% of FY17-20.

blocks.callout: **The capital question:** capex runs at ~9% of revenue (FY25-26), high for a business growing 15-20%. The new spending goes into products that should earn more than the core (ABS with in-house electronics, inverted front forks, 4W machined castings for export, battery packs), but each also comes with start-up costs, and battery packs carry a high material content. The European business needs capex just to hold its place as programmes move from combustion engines to hybrids and EVs.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean audit and strong cash conversion; incentives and acquisition accounting to watch

bullets: **Cash conversion is strong.** Cash from operations was ₹1,851 cr in FY26, 194% of profit and 94% of EBITDA (FY21-25: 60-99%). Suppliers fund working capital (payables ~100 days).

**State incentives sit in revenue.** ₹121 cr of Maharashtra PSI incentives were booked in FY26 revenue (~6% of EBITDA) and ₹35 cr in Q1FY27; the entitlement (₹858 cr) is finite and paid as state-GST refunds over ~7 years. Q4FY26's India margin fell 190bp partly because incentive bookings were 110bp lower.

**Other income is mostly treasury and miscellaneous items.** FY26 ₹124 cr: income from liquid/debt funds ₹30 cr (incl. ₹24 cr fair-value gains), interest ₹6 cr, foreign-exchange gain ₹16 cr and ₹66 cr of "miscellaneous income" (₹31 cr in FY25) that is not explained further. We forecast ₹115-125 cr without currency gains.

**Acquisition accounting.** Stöferle is consolidated at 100% with a ₹246 cr liability for the 40% Endurance does not yet own; its value depends on Stöferle's future EBITDA (assumed EUR18-21 mn) and is re-measured each year, which can move profit. Goodwill (Stöferle ₹349 cr, Maxwell ₹104 cr) is tested for impairment; the auditor flagged both as key audit matters.
**Exceptional items are small.** ₹21 cr labour-code charge in FY26; small gains in FY24-25. We forecast none.
**Depreciation choices move Europe's profit.** The accelerated write-off of ICE-programme assets (~EUR3 mn a quarter) lowers FY27-28 profit and raises it after; EBITDA is unaffected.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Unmodified audit by S R B C & Co. (EY network), strong cash conversion and no material related-party dealings with the promoters. The amber is for incentives inside revenue, a large unexplained "miscellaneous" other-income line, and the Stöferle put/call liability whose re-measurement can move profit.

sections.title: Net cash of ₹579 cr; suppliers fund the working capital

blocks.p: At Mar-2026 Endurance had ₹1,327 cr of borrowings (mostly in Europe, incl. Stöferle's) against ₹875 cr of cash and ₹1,031 cr of investments (mainly liquid and debt funds): net cash ₹579 cr. The India business alone had ₹416 cr of net cash at Jun-2026 even after paying >₹300 cr of commodity increases up front. Goodwill rose to ~₹729 cr (MOSL; Stöferle ₹349 cr and Maxwell ₹104 cr per the AR), and a ₹246 cr deferred consideration for the remaining 40% of Stöferle sits in other liabilities; 8% is bought each year from Jun-2026 (68% owned after Q1FY27). Working capital is close to zero: payables of ~100 days fund receivables (~46 days) and inventory (~50 days).

sections.title: Our honest summary: a well-run two-wheeler supplier priced at 27.8x Sep-28E EPS; HOLD

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's leading maker of two-wheeler suspension and brakes and a large aluminium caster, with net cash, a clean balance sheet and a credible pipeline of new content (ABS, inverted forks, alloy wheels, 4W castings, battery packs) that should keep India growing well ahead of vehicle volumes. Attached is a European castings business with high margins but no organic growth, and a dependence on Bajaj Auto for a third of income. Margins are set by metal prices and customers, not by Endurance.

**What you are paying:** 35.3x our FY27E and 29.5x FY28E EPS for ~14% a year EPS growth. Since 2021 the market has paid a median 31.3x forward for Endurance, and auto-component stocks were 7.8% below their five-year medians on 30-Sep-2026. On the street's own method and the house multiple the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): HOLD. The street's higher targets rest on higher EPS, not a higher multiple.

statementNotes.dep@Q1FY27: +35%: new plants and accelerated depreciation of Europe ICE-programme assets (EUR11.6 mn vs EUR8.5 mn).
statementNotes.sales@FY27E: GAM: India +23%, Europe +2% in euros (+9.5% in rupees), Maxwell +50%.
statementNotes.ebitdaMargin@FY27E: GAM: India margin 12.0% (11.2% in Q1, ~12.3% for Q2-Q4).
statementNotes.otherIncome@FY27E: GAM: treasury income ₹40 cr + recurring items ₹75 cr; no currency gains.
statementNotes.pat@FY28E: GAM: margin recovery in India and new plants at scale.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Endurance Technologies (consolidated, Rs crore). FY26 is the last reported year. Segment model on the company's entity basis: each entity's TOTAL INCOME and EBITDA as the company reports them (both include that entity's other income), plus consolidation adjustments, less consolidated other income as a negative line at 100% margin, so revenue and EBITDA tie to Screener's revenue (Rs14,596 cr) and operating profit (Rs1,966 cr); other income is then added back below EBITDA (built in _otherIncomeWhy). No minorities: Stöferle is consolidated at 100% with the put/call liability for the remaining stake booked as deferred consideration. Valued on P/E, as the street does; the multiple is derived in ENDURANCE.ctx.js and written here by ENDURANCE.val.js.

segments.name: India (ETL standalone)
segments._why: FY27E +23%: Q1FY27 +35.9% (of which ~12.9 points raw-material pass-through, ~23.5% underlying, q1call) on record 2W volumes (+23.6%); Q2-Q4 assumed ~+19% as the base absorbs the Sep-2025 GST cut from Q3 and new plants ramp (Bidkin alloy wheels to ~Rs600 cr a year by Q4FY27, Shendra castings >Rs200 cr in FY27, battery packs Rs300-360 cr, ABS doubling, Chennai brakes). FY28E +14% and FY29E +12%: 2W volumes +6-8% plus content (ABS regulation if notified, inverted forks, 4W castings to ~10% of sales, battery packs up to Rs600 cr in FY28, Shendra Rs513 cr peak in early FY29). Orders won since FY23: Rs5,270 cr peak value excl. Bajaj (Rs4,241 cr new).
segments._marginWhy: Company EBITDA margin incl. other income: 12.6% in FY26 (13.3% excl. Rs74 cr of non-value-add metal pass-through; Rs121 cr PSI incentives booked), 11.2% in Q1FY27 (RMC 68.4% vs 64.8%: Q1 billed on Q4 rates; Rs300 cr of commodity increases paid up front). Q2-Q3 'better than Q1' as Q1-average rates and conversion-cost claims flow through: Q2-Q4 ~12.3%, FY27E 12.0%. FY28E 12.6% and FY29E 12.8% as new plants pass start-up, still below FY25's 13.7% because pass-through inflates the denominator and battery packs carry lower margins. MOSL standalone ex other income: 10.9% Q1FY27, 11.5% FY27E.

segments.name: Maxwell (BMS electronics)
segments._why: FY26 Rs161 cr (+130%); Q1FY27 Rs57 cr (+85%; +21% QoQ). Cumulative orders Rs238 cr a year at peak by Q2FY28; RFQs >Rs300 cr. FY27E +50% (MOSL Rs238 cr), FY28E +30%, FY29E +25%.
segments._marginWhy: FY26 0.6% (Rs6 cr Hero Electric inventory provision in Q4); Q1FY27 7%, first PAT-positive quarter. 6% / 8% / 9%.

segments.name: Europe (Endurance Overseas incl. Stöferle)
segments._why: In euros: FY26 EUR391.7 mn (+28.9%; +2% ex Stöferle, parts +6.4%); Q1FY27 EUR104.3 mn (+1.1%) with EU production -5% and Chinese OEMs taking the growth. FY27E EUR ~400 mn (+2%, as MOSL), the Mercedes hybrid transmission part (100% share from Jan-2027, ~EUR40 mn a year) starting in Q4. FY28E +5% in euros (Mercedes full year, VW/Porsche castings) offset by ICE programmes ending (ICE ~30% of sales to 25% by FY28). FY29E +4%. Rupee held at the Q1FY27 rate (Rs110/EUR vs Rs102.6 in FY26), which adds ~7% to FY27E rupee growth; no further currency move assumed.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA margin incl. other income 18.4% in FY26 (EUR basis 18.5%), 18.2% in Q1FY27; energy prices in Italy +22% YoY (electricity) and gas +23% in Q1FY27. 18.0% / 18.3% / 18.3%: Stöferle integration benefits from Sep-2027 (management) offset by energy and volume risk. The Q1FY27 accelerated depreciation (EUR3 mn) is below EBITDA.

segments.name: Consolidation adjustments
segments._why: Inter-company sales (India to Europe castings, Maxwell BMS to ETL battery packs): -Rs154 cr in FY26, -Rs49 cr in Q1FY27 (-Rs33 cr). Grows with India.
segments._marginWhy: Elimination of unrealised margin: EBITDA -Rs3 cr on -Rs154 cr in FY26 (~2%).

segments.name: Less: other income (shown below EBITDA)
segments._why: The entity totals above include other income; this line removes consolidated other income (FY26 Rs124 cr) from revenue and EBITDA at 100%. It follows the otherIncome build: Rs115 / 120 / 125 cr.

assumptions._unallocLabel: None: corporate costs sit inside ETL standalone
assumptions._unallocWhy: Entity EBITDAs and adjustments add up to the company EBITDA; no separate corporate cost line.
assumptions._capexWhy: India ~Rs800 cr in FY27, similar to FY26's Rs828 cr (q4call, q1call; >80% expansion and dies). Europe EUR45 mn in FY26 (VW/Porsche, Stellantis, Daimler capacity); EUR3.6 mn in Q1FY27; we assume ~EUR35 mn (~Rs385 cr). FY26 consolidated capex ~Rs1,256 cr (MOSL). FY28E Rs1,250 cr and FY29E Rs1,300 cr (MOSL FY27-28E Rs1,250 cr each). Stöferle put/call payments (8% a year from Jun-2026, EUR6.24 mn paid in Q1FY27) settle a liability already booked and are not capex.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 D&A Rs734 cr (incl. Stöferle) on average gross block; Q1FY27 Rs222 cr incl. ~EUR3 mn accelerated depreciation of Europe ICE-programme assets (management: those assets are fully written off over ~18 months). The engine depreciates capex at once and holds CWIP flat; the rate gives FY27E ~Rs900 cr (MOSL Rs917 cr), FY28E ~Rs1,000 cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Treasury income is in the other-income build below (on gross cash and investments, not on net cash).
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built, not plugged (AR FY26 note 19: Rs124 cr): (1) treasury income on ~Rs1,900 cr of gross cash and current investments at ~2% after tax-efficient debt funds: Rs40 cr (FY26 Rs36 cr: interest Rs6 cr + income from current investments Rs30 cr; FY25 Rs60 cr); (2) recurring non-operating income Rs75 / 80 / 85 cr (miscellaneous Rs66 cr, asset-sale gains Rs5 cr, write-backs Rs1 cr in FY26); (3) no foreign-exchange gain (Rs16 cr in FY26). FY27E Rs115 cr vs TTM to Jun-2026 Rs121 cr before the labour-code charge (Screener Rs100 cr net of it) and Q1FY27 Rs33 cr; MOSL FY27E Rs139 cr.
assumptions._interestLabel: Finance cost (borrowings, leases and unwinding of the Stöferle deferred consideration)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs57 cr; Q1FY27 Rs17 cr. Borrowings Rs1,327 cr at Mar-2026 (mostly Europe, incl. Stöferle's) plus the Rs246 cr deferred consideration for the remaining 40% of Stöferle. FY27E Rs70 cr (Q1 run-rate), easing as Europe repays debt (MOSL Rs65 / 61 cr).

dcf._betaWhy: Cyclical auto supplier with net cash and 35% of income from one customer: beta 1.0, cost of equity 12.5%. Net cash, so the cost of equity is the discount rate.
dcf._tgWhy: India's nominal GDP grows ~10%; 2W volumes ~5-6% a year plus content; Europe flat to low growth. House range 5-6%: 6%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~11% in FY29E to 8% over 15 years.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin (ex other income) fades to 13.5%: FY22-26 range 11.8-13.5%; no pricing power beyond pass-through.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex 5% of revenue at maturity (FY22-26 average ~8.5% in a heavy build-out incl. Europe); depreciation 4.5% of revenue (FY26 5.0%).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: 2W volumes keep growing high single digits after the GST step; ABS becomes mandatory for smaller bikes; battery packs, Shendra and Bidkin ramp on time; commodity costs ease and pass-through catches up, lifting India margins back to ~13.5%; Europe holds share as Chinese OEMs localise sourcing.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: 2W volumes flatten against the GST base; Bajaj Auto (35% of income) loses share or in-sources; commodity and energy costs are recovered late; Europe loses ICE programmes faster than hybrid/EV orders replace them and energy prices squeeze margins.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Endurance: P/E on one-year-forward EPS (MOSL 32x FY28E, Choice 30x FY28E, JM Financial 32x FY28E at initiation). Multiple derived in ENDURANCE.ctx.js and written by ENDURANCE.val.js.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Own trailing EV/EBITDA median since Apr-2021 with the same sector de-rating, restated to Sep-28E EBITDA.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, cost of equity 12.5%, terminal growth 6%, plus net cash.

oiBuild._note: Other income build (Rs crore), checked against otherIncome and the oi segment in ENDURANCE.ctx.js
